title: ResetAndRewire broadcasts with --skip-simulation and a non-idempotent step sequence: the YS-01 deposit revert lands mid-suite on mainnet, leaving pools Active/strategyless/unpaused with no re-run path through the entry point
description: The broadcast entry uses --skip-simulation --slow, so forge sends txs one-by-one without a pre-broadcast bundle simulation. With the strategies as actually deployed (YS-01: previewRedeem reverts under STATICCALL), the mainnet run executes tx1 finalizeAndReset(DOLA) and tx2 finalizeAndReset(USDC) successfully then halts at tx3 setYieldStrategy(DOLA, ysDolaV2) with an on-chain reverted tx. Halt state: both pools revived to Active with yieldStrategy == address(0), migrator still migrator1, idle 26.785 DOLA + 27.234 USDC unswept, and 9 users parked yield-less in the temp staker. The entry point is NOT re-runnable after fixing the strategies: finalizeAndReset requires PoolState.Migrating, so tx1 reverts on every retry — and with --skip-simulation each retry burns another reverted mainnet tx. Worse, the halt window is publicly exposed: neither staker is paused and stake() on an Active strategyless pool succeeds, so ANY deposit (innocent or a 1-wei grief, ledger ss10l1) sets totalStaked > 0 and re-locks setYieldStrategy behind the story-010 empty-pool gate, forcing a full second terminal-migration cycle. A default forge simulation (no --skip-simulation) would have simulated the 6-tx bundle, hit the tx3 revert, and refused to send anything.
impact: Protocol availability + operational hazard, no direct fund loss: migration suite halts half-configured on mainnet; user principal stranded (recoverable) in temp until manual out-of-runbook recovery; recovery itself griefable via the story-010 gate during the unpaused halt window.

classification.assetImpact: No direct fund loss but the most severe halt-state: --skip-simulation lands the YS-01 deposit revert mid-suite on mainnet after tx1/tx2 succeed, leaving both pools Active with yieldStrategy==0, migrator still migrator1, ~27 DOLA + ~27 USDC idle unswept, and 9 users parked yield-less in temp. The entry point is not re-runnable (finalizeAndReset requires Migrating) and the unpaused halt window is griefable.
attackPath: 1. Broadcast with --skip-simulation --slow sends txs one-by-one with no pre-bundle simulation.
2. tx1/tx2 finalizeAndReset succeed; tx3 setYieldStrategy reverts (YS-01 brick) on-chain mid-suite.
3. Pools left Active/strategyless/unpaused; finalizeAndReset reverts on every retry (one-shot), burning more reverted txs.

4. Anyone deposits 1 wei (or innocent stake) into the Active strategyless pool -> totalStaked>0 re-locks setYieldStrategy behind the story-010 empty-pool gate, forcing a full second terminal-migration cycle.
classification.likelihood: Plausible given YS-01 is deterministic; the gate-relock grief is a cheap permissionless action during the public halt window.
classification.assumptions: Recovery is out-of-runbook and itself griefable; a default forge simulation would have caught the tx3 revert and sent nothing.
classification.externalRequirements: An (innocent or malicious) deposit in the unpaused halt window to trigger the gate-relock amplification.

evidence: side-effects.json unmodifiedPreview (revert at tx3 with tx1/tx2 succeeding); StableStaker.finalizeAndReset require(poolState==Migrating) (StableStaker.sol:594); paused()==false on both stakers at post-state; story-010 gate at StableStaker.setYieldStrategy:228.
recommendation: 1) Drop --skip-simulation from all ys-swap broadcast entries. 2) Make the script resumable: guard each step (skip finalizeAndReset when poolState already Active; skip setMigrator when already set). 3) Pause both stakers for the migration window to close the public-stake gate-relock during any halt. 4) Run the preview variant against live mainnet immediately before broadcast as a hard runbook gate.
